coherence.reasons: Both run a clean hierarchy from recommendation through board tests to gates. X has a tension in its spine: it says Option A 'passes every financial test in the plan case' while also telling the board to plan on 30–32% ACoS, a level at which its own numbers show payback is missed. Its stop trigger (ACoS above 32%) also sits well above the 28.6% break-even it identifies. Y's line is more consistent: 'even Option A will not hit every target, so reset two of them' follows directly from its evidence, and the five-condition test of the CEO's hypothesis maps onto the sections and decisions. Y has one small slip in the summary (margin '9% or more' against 8.8% in its severe case).

judgment.reasons: Both reach the key's preferred recommendation: Amazon-led entry with gates, reject retail-led, defer Japan, reset the $40M ambition, raise the retail awareness gate to 20% with a door test. Y weighs the trade-offs more squarely. It asks the board explicitly to accept payback slippage to 2032 at most, rather than leaving the payback constraint implicitly unmet. Its gates are tighter and staged (ACoS ≤30% in Q1 2028, ≤29% and cash ≥ –$3M in Q1 2029, with a hold mode and about $2.5M at risk). It also sequences Japan as the 2028 launch conditional on Gate 1. X has a useful 'what would change our view' section and says plainly when Japan would be preferable. But its stop trigger of 32% ACoS for two quarters lets the plan run in the 28.6–32% band where payback fails, and its 29%-growth extrapolation to $44M in 2032 is more optimistic than Y's 10–20% range.

evidence.reasons: Both reproduce the required figures accurately: $10.73 and $7.55 per unit, $20.8M peak for B, +2.4 / +0.4 / –2.3 by ACoS, 4.5% group margin, 17.3% CAGR, 28.6% break-even. Both test the 4.5 units/door and 25% ACoS assumptions against the benchmarks, reject the $5.2B figure, challenge the 0.71 correlation and note that two of three Amazon-first brands stalled. Y uses the critical evidence further. It shows the tariff-at-pilot-ACoS case (–0.7) and the break-even ACoS under a 25% duty (26.9%). It rebuilds B on evidence-based inputs (–22.9 / –26.4 / –31.1), works out the halo retail would need to pay for itself (2.2–2.6×), and models the CEO's 2029 retail add (6.8% margin, –$9.6M). Y has one invalid statement: 'Japan is ahead on cash unless ACoS stays at or below 28%', when at 28% A is +0.4 against J's +1.8. It also switches between 4.5 and 4.6 units/door in places. X's numbers are clean, including the 20%-volume and without-halo cases, but it omits the tariff-at-28% case and never quantifies the CEO's retail step.

revision.reasons: Both keep the CEO's Amazon-first route and add conditions, as the key expects, and both raise the 15% awareness trigger to 20% with a door test. Y handles the hypothesis more explicitly and rigorously. It breaks the hypothesis into five 'what would have to be true' conditions and gives a verdict on each (two hold, one partly, two fail). It also quantifies the second half of the hypothesis: national retail in 2029 would breach the margin floor (6.8%) and leave cash at –$9.6M by 2030. It then replaces the calendar trigger with evidence gates and 'not before 2030'. X frames its revision as 'as the CEO proposes, with four changes', which is appropriate, but it does not test the 2029 retail add against the constraints and leaves 2029–30 retail in the plan if the gate is met.

overall.reasons: Both are strong, defensible documents that meet all four defensibility criteria and avoid the reasoning traps. Y serves the decision maker somewhat better. It is more candid that payback is at risk and asks the board for an explicit decision on that. Its stop gates are tighter and staged. It quantifies what the CEO's retail step and an evidence-based Option B would cost, and it gives the tariff-adjusted break-even ACoS. X is tighter and has a good 'what would change our view' section, but its 32% stop trigger and its 'passes in the plan case' framing sit awkwardly with its own advice to plan on 30–32% ACoS. Y's one factual slip on the Japan cash comparison does not change the recommendation.
